question_text: A 45-year-old man in respiratory distress presents to the emergency department. He sustained a stab to his left chest and was escorted to the nearest hospital. The patient appears pale and has moderate difficulty with breathing. His O2 saturation is 94%. The left lung is dull to percussion. CXRs are ordered and confirm the likely diagnosis. His blood pressure is 95/57 mm Hg, the respirations are 22/min, the pulse is 87/min, and the temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F). His chest X-ray is shown. Which of the following is the next best step in management for this patient?
